{{Quote|A Dark Jedi, on the other hand, has much smaller ambitions. He&mdash;or she&mdash;thinks only of himself. He acts alone. The ultimate goal is not galactic conquest, but personal wealth and importance. Like a common thug or criminal, he revels in cruelty and selfishness. He preys upon the weak and vulnerable, spreading misery and suffering wherever he goes.|[[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obba]]|<ref name="Darth Bane: Dynasty of Evil">''[[Darth Bane: Dynasty of Evil]]''</ref>}}
'''Dark Jedi''', also known as '''"Fallen" Jedi''', were [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitives]], frequently former [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], who chose to deny the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side of the Force]] or follow the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]. Although "Dark Jedi" originally referred to a Jedi who had fallen to the dark side, it could also refer to uninitiated Force-sensitives who received no [[Jedi training/Legends|Jedi training]] but began their careers under another Dark Jedi. Others were simply dark-side users who did not follow the teachings of the Sith or other [[darksider]] organizations. In some cases, Dark Jedi also included "artificial" [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-sensitives who served the dark side, such as the [[Reborn]] and the [[Shadowtrooper]]s. The first Dark Jedi was [[Rajivari]]. Other forerunners included [[Xendor]], who lead the [[Legions of Lettow]] during the [[First Great Schism]], and [[Ajunta Pall]] and [[Exiles|his followers]] who, after the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]], were exiled from [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] space and became the ancient progenitors of the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]]. Ultimately, the title became something of a blanket term for darksiders who could not be classified as belonging to any specific dark side organization.

Dark Jedi also became a term of note during the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]] and the [[Jedi Civil War]], where fallen Jedi served under the banners of [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] and the duo of [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] and [[Darth Malak]], respectively. Thousands of years later, Sith Lords such as [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] would resurrect the term, with agents serving under him bearing the title. Those whom the [[Miraluka/Legends|Miraluka]] [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]] controlled came to be known as the [[Seven Dark Jedi]].

==Description==
Dark Jedi were [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] that had fallen under the sway of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. Jedi were susceptible to the lure of the dark side at any time. As [[Padawan/Legends|Padawans]], the call of the dark side was always a temptation until they were fully [[Jedi training/Legends|trained]]. But even experienced Jedi could turn from the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]] and embrace the dark side.<ref name="RPG-Core">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook]]''</ref>

==Relationship to the Sith==
{{Quote|You wear the trappings of the Sith, you fight like the Sith&hellip; but this can be imitated, however. You lack a vital quality found in all Sith. Sith have no fear, and I sense much fear in you.|[[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] and [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]]|<ref name="Chapter 6">{{CW|6}}</ref>}}
Despite the fact that both groups called upon the dark side of the Force, Dark Jedi were not the same as the Sith, although [[Exiles|one group of Dark Jedi]] were the predecessors of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lords]] of the ancient [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]].<ref name="JvS" />

[[File:Dark_Side_Master_TotG.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A Dark side Master in an apparent [[Form III/Legends|Soresu]] stance]]
The term ''Dark Jedi'' was a collective and vague name of dark-side practitioners (be they fallen or rogue Jedi) that used [[Force power/Legends|Force powers]] and a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], but were not always members of a certain organization, whereas the term ''Sith'' referred to a definite heritage or ideology. Some Dark Jedi were allied to the Sith or other organizations, while others were loners. Because they were notoriously dangerous, unstable, and treacherous, Dark Jedi seldom formed well-organized groups on their own in order to expand their following or reinforce their strength. One notable exception to this was the [[Miraluka/Legends|Miraluka]] Dark Jedi [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]] and his retinue of [[Seven Dark Jedi|minions]]. Dark Jedi could also use their power for personal gain, becoming mercenaries or assassins.

The Sith, however, was an order that followed their [[Code of the Sith/Legends|code]] and studied their history, studied their own skills and techniques, and possessed knowledge such as [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]]. Furthermore, after the [[Rule of Two/Legends|Rule of Two]] was established, the [[Order of the Sith Lords]] was limited to only two members, a [[Sith Master/Legends|master]], and an [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], whereas the Dark Jedi had no organization and no such limitations.<ref name="JvS" />

The Sith often seduced Dark Jedi to work for them, without really granting them any knowledge of Sith techniques. Yet most Dark Jedi were willing to serve the Sith and saw it as a way to further their knowledge of the Force. Like those of the Sith, their lightsabers usually had red blades, but were also known to have a wide variety of colors.

Many dark-side practitioners, such as [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], considered the power of a Dark Jedi to be nothing compared to the power of the Sith. According to Dooku, a prime difference between Dark Jedi and Sith is that the Sith "lack fear."<ref name="Chapter 6" />

==History of the Dark Jedi==
===The [[Old Republic era]]===
====The [[First Great Schism]] and early Dark Jedi====
{{Quote|They called themselves the Legions of Lettow, and they were led by General Xendor, a powerful Force-using humanoid whose origins remain unknown.|[[Tionne Solusar]]|<ref name="JvS" />}}
After the Jedi Order was established, divisions began to appear within the order's structure, leading to the [[First Great Schism]], (c. [[24,500 BBY]]), when several [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] were discovered using the "dark" side of the Force. The Dark Jedi [[Xendor]] and his followers, the [[Legions of Lettow]], allied with the master of [[Teräs Käsi/Legends|Teräs Käsi]] [[Arden Lyn]]<ref name="JvS" /> and her [[Followers of Palawa]]<ref name="complete">{{CSWECite|II|268|Lyn, Arden}}</ref> from [[Bunduki/Legends|Bunduki]].<ref name="JvS" /> In a [[Battle of Columus|climactic battle]], [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Awdrysta Pina]] slew Xendor. Soon afterwards, the rest of these dissidents were [[Battle of Lettow|defeated]],<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> Pina [[Duel on Irkalla|stopped Lyn's heart]] with [[Morichro/Legends|morichro]],<ref name="JvS" /> and Lyn used the [[Kashi Mer talisman]] to kill Pina.<ref name="EGW" />

Dark Jedi of the time were considered to be apostates, with many hiding on the edges of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] away from the eyes of their former comrades. These Dark Jedi inhabited the lawless places of the galaxy, relying on their talents for survival and to amass power and glory.<ref name="RPG-Core" />

====The [[Second Great Schism]] and the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]]====
{{Quote|The Dark Jedi, finally defeated after a century of bloodshed, took their battered ships into exile&hellip;|[[Odan-Urr/Legends|Odan-Urr]]|<ref name="TOTJ 0">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 0|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 0]]</ref>}}
For over the next seventeen millennia, crises involving the Dark Jedi were rather isolated. One example involved a female [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] named [[Halbret]] who had brought together a contingent of Jedi Knights during the [[Pius Dea Era]] to defeat a powerful Dark Jedi who had enslaved the [[Kathol (species)|Kathol]] species.

Around [[7000 BBY]], however, a [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|second war]] broke out between the Jedi and Dark Jedi that lasted a hundred years. The Dark Jedi were finally defeated at the [[Battle of Corbos]] and exiled into the far reaches of space. These exiles finally landed on the planet [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], enslaved the native [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]], and eventually interbred with them and created a new [[:Category:Dark side organizations|Force organization]] that eventually would plague the galaxy for millennia: the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] cult.<ref name="JvS" />

====The [[Golden Age of the Sith]] and the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]]====
The Dark Jedi exiles and the Sith species formed an [[Sith Empire/Legends|immensely rich and powerful empire]] built upon sorcery and dark-side-fueled technology.<ref name="TOTJ 2">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 2]]</ref> Over the subsequent 1900 years,<ref name="JvS" /> the Sith Empire and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] thrived in isolation from the each other.<ref name="TOTJ 2" />

In [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], after [[Marka Ragnos]], the reigning [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] died, two other [[Sith Lord]]s, [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]] and [[Ludo Kressh]], clashed for the mantle of Dark Lord. Two explorers from the Republic, [[Jori Daragon|Jori]] and [[Gav Daragon]], stumbled upon Korriban and the Sith Empire.<ref name="TOTJ 2" /> They were imprisoned upon arrival and the [[Sith Council]] decided to execute them. Naga Sadow secretly freed the Daragons and made it appear that the Republic freed them.<ref name="TOTJ 3">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 3|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 3]]</ref>

Believing that the Republic had broken the Daragons out of prison,<ref name="TOTJ 3" /> the Sith coronated Sadow as their new Dark Lord<ref name="TOTJ 4">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 4]]</ref> and attacked the Republic.<ref name="TOTJ F3">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 3|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 3]]</ref>

====The [[Third Great Schism]] and the [[Vultar Cataclysm]]====
In [[4250 BBY]], the [[Third Great Schism]] broke out on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], which led to the destruction of the Dark Jedi of that conflict in the [[Vultar Cataclysm]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>

====The [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]]====
Many Jedi seduced by [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] became Dark Jedi. After the death of Kun, many Dark Jedi still existed and served under new Sith Lords like [[Darth Malak]] and [[Darth Nihilus]].<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

====The [[Jedi Civil War]]====
[[File:KotOR_Dark_Jedi.png|thumb|right|200px|A typical Dark Jedi during the [[Jedi Civil War]].]]
Many Jedi joined [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] and Malak when they joined the [[Mandalorian Wars]], and almost all of them became Dark Jedi when the Jedi Civil War started. Jedi who hadn't followed them were captured and turned to the dark side, becoming Dark Jedi themselves.<ref name="TSL">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>

====The [[Fourth Great Schism]] & The [[New Sith Wars]]====
In [[2000 BBY/Legends|2000 BBY]], [[Umbaran/Legends|Umbaran]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Darth Ruin/Legends|Phanius]] fell to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]. He left the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] with fifty Jedi Knights and became Darth Ruin. He eventually established a [[new Sith]] Empire that later resulted in the [[New Sith Wars]]. During the era of Lord [[Skere Kaan]], many dark-siders were considered Sith Lords and very few Dark Jedi were ever seen in the following millennia, until the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="JvS" />

===The [[Republic Classic era]]===
In approximately [[600 BBY/Legends|600 BBY]], fallen Jedi Knight [[Allya/Legends|Allya]] was banished to [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]], where she became the founder of the [[Witches of Dathomir]].<ref name="NEC" />

In [[188 BBY]], a [[Dark Jedi Conflict]] occurred in the [[Cularin system/Legends|Cularin system]], led by fallen [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Kibh Jeen]].<ref name="JvS" />

Jedi Master [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn's]] Padawan [[Xanatos]] turned to the dark side and later died in a confrontation with his master.<ref name="NEC" />

At some point, a being named [[Lycan]] left the Jedi Order and became a Dark Jedi. He also introduced his [[Iktotchi/Legends|Iktotchi]] apprentice, [[Sardoth]], to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. [[32 BBY/Legends|In 32 BBY]], following a starcruiser crash, he lost his memory and went on an aimless killing spree. He was eventually tracked to the planet Molivar and killed in an ambush set by [[Darca Nyl]], a retired mercenary whose family Lycan had slain.

On [[Ahakista/Legends|Ahakista]] in [[0 ABY/Legends|9 months ABY]], Sardoth confronted Nyl, vowing to retrieve his dead master's blade. However, Darth Vader, sensing the presence of a force user not aligned with The Galactic Empire, intervened and killed Sardoth.

A few years before the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invasion]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] by the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|droid army]] of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], a [[Marauding Dark Jedi|group]] of Dark Jedi brought terror to the [[Elrood sector/Legends|Elrood sector]]. Their reign of fear ended when the [[Jedi Ambassador]] [[Jorus C'baoth]] and his strike team defeated the darksiders.<ref name="RPGRCR">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Revised Core Rulebook]]''</ref>

===Clone Wars===
{{Main|Dark Acolyte/Legends}}
[[File:ChronicallyCW-HC66-AsajjVentresscloak.png|thumb|left|220px|[[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]], one of [[Dooku/Legends|Darth Tyranus']] [[Dark Acolyte/Legends|Dark Acolytes]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].]]
After the apparent death of [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] apprenticed [[Dooku/Legends|Darth Tyranus]], who in turn apprenticed [[Dark Acolyte/Legends|several]] Dark Jedi, including [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] and [[Sora Bulq/Legends|Sora Bulq]]. He also supposedly had under his wing the Jedi-turned-Dark Jedi [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]].

During the war, the [[Bpfassh]] Dark Jedi crisis occurred. A group of [[Bpfasshi/Legends|Bpfasshi]] Dark Jedi were responsible for a rampage of terror and destruction throughout the [[Bpfassh system/Legends|Bpfassh system]] and, indeed, the entire [[Sluis sector/Legends|Sluis sector]]. A Jedi task force led by [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] was sent to stop them and quell the uprising.<ref name="NEC" />

Near the end of the Clone Wars, everything went wrong for Dooku. Ventress, after faking her own death, fled to an unknown location. Sora Bulq was killed by Quinlan, after the latter had turned back to the light, during the [[Siege of Saleucami/Legends|Siege of Saleucami]]. Another Dark Jedi named [[Tol Skorr]] was also killed by Quinlan during the battle. A few weeks after the siege, Dooku himself was killed by Anakin Skywalker onboard [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous's]] flagship, the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']]. Soon after, Skywalker became Darth Vader, Sidious' newest apprentice, and the Sith ruled the galaxy once more. This would lead to the employment of many more Dark Jedi.

===Galactic Empire===
{{Main|Dark side adept/Legends}}
{{Quote|I have watched you. You have advanced in submission to my will. I will make you '''Dark Jedi'''&mdash;extensions of my own power.|Reborn [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] to [[Xecr Nist]] and [[Tedryn-Sha]]|<ref name="DEII 4">[[Dark Empire II 4|''Dark Empire II'' 4]]</ref>}}
[[File:Serpent_Shard_GH_by_Shoemaker.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[Illiv Orfa]], Dark Jedi on Mustafar]]
With the Jedi effectively extinct, Dark Jedi were also a lot rarer.<ref name="RPG-Core" /> During the span of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Sidious established a number of organizations composed by Dark Jedi, including the [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitorius]], the [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hands]], and his personal [[Dark Side Elite]]. Many [[Agricultural Corps/Legends|AgriCorps]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawans]] were captured by Vader after the execution of [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]]. The younglings that Vader did not kill (which were very few) were trained in the ways of the dark side by several [[Dark side adept/Legends|Dark Side Adepts]], including Vader himself. After Vader's death, Sidious would not risk living with another apprentice after losing ''three'', and so the [[Dark Side Elite]] became the right hand of Darth Sidious during [[Operation Shadow Hand]]. Sidious also trained several [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hands]], special assassins that did his bidding. Famous ones included Darth Vader's daughter-in-law, [[Mara Jade Skywalker]], and [[Lumiya|Shira Brie]], who would later become Lumiya, Vader's apprentice. Mara was later redeemed by her future husband, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], and became a Jedi Master.

===Post-Palpatine era===
{{Main|Reborn}}
{{Quote|He is a Dark Jedi.''"<br />"''Jedi?"<br />"''Dark'' Jedi.|[[8t88/Legends|8t88]] and [[Kyle Katarn]], discussing the Dark Jedi [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]]|<ref name="JK">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Desann_and_Jerec.jpg|thumb|left|170px|[[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitor]] [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]] & [[Desann]].]]
After the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], Dark Jedi sporadically appeared throughout the years.

One group of Dark Jedi rallied under [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]] in an effort to locate and siphon the power of the [[Valley of the Jedi]]. This faction, often known as the [[Seven Dark Jedi]], was defeated by [[Kyle Katarn]].<ref name="JK" />

As [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] established his [[Jedi Praxeum]] and established the [[New Jedi Order]], some of his students began to bridle at the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master's]] inflexibility. Some would inevitably fall prey to the temptations of the dark side and become Dark Jedi.<ref name="RPG-Core" />

In the [[Empire Reborn]] campaign, [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Hethrir]], [[Desann]], and [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Galak Fyyar]] created an unusual hybrid of Dark Jedi and [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] by giving them [[Cortosis/Legends|cortosis]]-weave armor and crystals from [[Artus Prime]]. These soldiers were called the [[shadowtrooper]]s. [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]-in-training Kyle Katarn and his partner [[Jan Ors]] put a stop to the project and defeated two of the three heads.

In [[14 ABY/Legends|14 ABY]], Master Katarn and his new apprentices, [[Jaden Korr]] and [[Rosh Penin]], came to the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic's]] rescue as Desann's former apprentice, [[Tavion Axmis]], discovered the [[Scepter of Ragnos]] and created a new [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] cult called the [[Disciples of Ragnos]]. The cult consisted of [[Sith cultist/Legends|cultists]] and Desann's old [[Reborn]] warriors, and was also allied to the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]]. The Disciples and Tavion were defeated by Korr and Katarn, and Rosh was redeemed after joining.

A young Jedi named [[Kueller|Dolph]] trained under the New Jedi Order for less than a year before returning home and finding his parents' dead bodies impaled before the governmental palace, having been slain by the Je'har government. He became the Dark Jedi Kueller and used his powers to bring down the Je'har regime. He then orchestrated the [[Almanian Uprising]], only to be thwarted by Jedi Master [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and his sister [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]].<ref name="The New Rebellion">''[[The New Rebellion]]''</ref>

Many Dark Jedi would later become part of the [[Second Imperium]]. Led by a former Jedi named [[Brakiss]], the second Imperium assaulted Luke Skywalker's [[Jedi academy]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]. Brakiss was eventually defeated by Skywalker then killed when a [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Royal Guardsman]] triggered an explosive device after nearly being killed by him, thus destroying the Second Imperium.

[[Irek Ismaren]] was built into the cyborg Dark Jedi, Lord Nyax. Lord Nyax was eventually defeated by Luke Skywalker, Mara Jade Skywalker, and Tahiri Veila.<ref name="Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand">''[[The New Jedi Order: Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand]]''</ref>

During the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Yuuzhan Vong War|war]] and the [[Gorog|Dark Nest]] crisis, scarcely any Dark Jedi remained. The only apparent Dark Jedi during these crises were Nightsister [[Lomi Plo]] and [[Shadow Academy]] student [[Welk]]. Both were killed by Luke Skywalker during the Dark Nest crisis, however, both were secretly members of the [[One Sith]]. Also, a former Jedi named [[Alema Rar]] became a Dark Jedi during the [[Dark Nest Crisis]], but was supposedly killed during [[Battle of Tenupe|one of its final battles]]. Alema was later proven alive but grievously not wounded, only to die later by the hands of Jagged Fel.

Despite all these tragic deaths and defeats, the Dark Lady Lumiya eventually resurfaced as a Sith, but was eventually killed by Luke Skywalker, who believed that she had murdered his wife Mara.<ref name="Sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Would you have preferred we have brought back a full-fledged Dark Jedi? A second Darth Vader, perhaps, with the sort of ambitions and power that might easily lead him to take over your ship? Count your blessings, Captain."''<br />''"At least a Dark Jedi would have been predictable.|Grand Admiral Thrawn to Captain Gilad Pellaeon, discussing Joruus C'baoth|<ref name="Heir to the Empire">''[[Heir to the Empire]]''</ref>}}
''Star Wars'' author [[Timothy Zahn]] coined the term "Dark Jedi" in his [[1991]] novel ''[[Heir to the Empire]]''. Zahn needed a label for a Jedi who had fallen to the dark side, and the term "Sith" would not be properly defined for another few years. He went with "Dark Jedi," which he regarded as "descriptive if not very original."

Over time, the definition of the term became progressively less precise, and "Dark Jedi" ended up referring to both fallen Jedi and malevolent Force users who never underwent proper training.<ref name="HE20">''[[Heir to the Empire: The 20th Anniversary Edition]]''</ref> Perhaps due to uneven usage within [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] sources, many fans have argued that "Dark Jedi" describes only those dark-side users who had previously been a Jedi or were once being trained as a member of the Order. [[Leland Chee]] dispelled this notion in two posts on the [[StarWars.com]] [[StarWars.com Message Boards|forums]]:
{{Quote|We avoid [Dark Jedi] when we can. Dark Jedi definition still refers to any dark side user.|Leland Chee|<ref name="SWB 1">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=222689&start=4050#16245404|thread=Welcome some BCaT VIPs|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2007-01-31|time=11:32 AM}}</ref>}}
{{Quote|A dark Jedi is anyone who practices the dark side of the Force whether or not they were a former Jedi.|Leland Chee|<ref name="SWB 2">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=219272&tstart=175#10894723|thread=Dark Jedi in the EU&hellip;|author=[[Leland Chee]]|date=2005-05-21|time=2:09 AM}}</ref>}}
